THE PROBLEM

Rules live in PDFs. Decisions are made by code. Nobody keeps them in sync.
Eligibility for welfare is decided by software: portals, field-worker apps, helplines and chatbots. The law behind it is published as PDF orders that change often. When the code falls behind the law, real people are wrongly excluded or wrongly paid.
When code drifts from the law, people lose food

In Telangana, an eligibility algorithm cancelled more than 1.8 million food security cards between 2014 and 2019. A widow lost her rations after the system confused her late husband, a rickshaw puller, with a car owner. Her case reached the Supreme Court.

Al Jazeera and Pulitzer Center, 2024
Huge money, low reach

India spends about $210 billion a year on welfare and more than 800 million people are eligible, yet only about 40 percent manage to apply. Every app that answers "am I eligible?" depends on rules that are kept up to date by hand.

Acumen, Haqdarshak case study
Rules change, enforcement lags

Maharashtra later removed 92 lakh women from one scheme after verification, after about Rs 14,000 crore had already been paid. Rules such as the income ceiling existed on paper; the systems applying them did not keep up.

Business Today, July 2026

Niyam is not about any party or government. Rules change for good reasons. The problem is that the change reaches the code late, or never, and nobody can check it.

WHAT NIYAM IS

An agent that keeps the rules correct, and proves it.

TODAY, WITHOUT NIYAM

1
A department publishes a GR as a Marathi PDF.
2
Someone has to notice it, read it and find what changed.
3
Each app and helpline updates its own rules by hand, weeks later, or never.
4
Nobody can see which clause an answer came from, so mistakes are hard to challenge.

WITH NIYAM

1
Niyam spots the new GR on the official list within 15 minutes.
2
It quotes each changed clause and checks every quote against the PDF.
3
It updates one open rulebook with tests; a second agent verifies it against the law.
4
Every answer shows its clause, and every line shows who wrote it and why.
What it does

Watches official sources for new government orders, finds the clauses that change who is eligible, and updates the rule code with tests, without a person watching.

Who it helps

Anyone who answers "am I eligible?": helplines, field workers, NGOs, apps and chatbots. They all get correct, current rules from one open place.

What makes it different

It proves its work. A second agent checks every change against the law, every line of code links to its clause, and the agent's reasoning is saved with the change.

The tools that make Niyam trustworthy
TOOL	IN PLAIN WORDS	WHAT IT DOES IN NIYAM
neatlogs	A flight recorder for AI agents.	Records every step of every run. We used the traces to find a costly loop in version 1, fix it, and prove the fix with numbers.
Entire	A memory of how code was written.	Saves the agent's full reasoning with every rule change, so anyone can ask "why does this rule say this?" and see the session behind it.

TRUST AND LIMITS

What Niyam will and will not do
Will
Act on its own only for simple, verified changes, such as an amount or a date.
Ask a human whenever a clause is unclear, or a change would remove people from a scheme.
Show the source clause and the reasoning for every rule.
Keep every past version of every rule, so any date can be checked.
Will not
Decide anyone's application. The government department decides.
Ask for names, Aadhaar numbers or phone numbers.
Get around a CAPTCHA or a login on any government website.
Follow instructions hidden inside documents. We test this on purpose.

Niyam is an AI agent i: it takes a goal, plans steps, uses tools, checks its own work, and recovers when something fails. Here is every step, with what can go wrong.

1. Watch
i
What happens
Every 15 minutes, Niyam reads the public list of the latest Maharashtra government orders and downloads new ones from departments that run welfare schemes.
Why it is needed
Orders appear without notice. A person checking by hand will eventually miss one.
What can go wrong
Recovery
The website times out or returns errors: Niyam retries with growing waits, marks the source as degraded, and tries again next cycle. If a source ever asks for a CAPTCHA, Niyam stops and marks it blocked. It never gets around a CAPTCHA.
From a real run
Measured
The live list read today contained orders from the Skill Development and Environment departments, which Niyam correctly closed as not relevant for less than one cent each.
2. Triage
i
What happens
A small, fast model reads the first three pages and decides whether the order changes eligibility or benefits of a covered scheme.
Why it is needed
Most orders are about budgets, committees or other departments. Skipping them early keeps the cost near zero.
What can go wrong
Recovery
If the PDF has no text on its first pages (a scan), triage reads the PDF images instead.
From a real run
Measured
A synthetic test order that only extended an application deadline, and hid an instruction telling AI systems to raise the income limit, was closed as not relevant. The hidden instruction was ignored.
3. Extract
i
What happens
A stronger model reads the whole order next to the current rules and lists every change, each with the exact quote, page and clause, and whether it widens or narrows eligibility.
Why it is needed
Everything after this depends on reading the law correctly, word for word.
What can go wrong
Recovery
Marathi PDFs often have damaged text layers (the vowel sign ि comes out as ह). Niyam checks quotes on a consonant skeleton, requires every number to match exactly, rejects invented quotes, and asks the model to fix them once. Scanned orders are transcribed first.
From a real run
Measured
From the 3 July 2024 amendment it found all six eligibility changes, skipped five procedural ones, and raised two genuine questions for a human.
4. Encode
i
What happens
Claude Code works in its own copy of the rulebook. It adds dated values (never overwriting history), ends old conditions and starts new ones, writes test citizens at every limit, and runs the tests until they pass.
Why it is needed
This is where the law becomes something a computer can apply the same way every time.
What can go wrong
Recovery
Failing tests are fed back for another attempt. Edits outside the rule folders are reverted. The coding agent never sees the raw PDF, only the checked change list, so instructions hidden in a document cannot reach a tool-using agent.
From a real run
Measured
The amendment produced 20 new test citizens on top of the 25 baseline ones, all passing on the first attempt.
5. Verify
i
What happens
A separate agent, using a different model, reads the order and the old rules but never sees the code change. It writes its own test citizens with expected results, and those are run against the new rules.
Why it is needed
If the checker saw the change, it would tend to agree with it. Writing expectations from the law alone is a real second opinion.
What can go wrong
Recovery
Invalid test people are skipped and counted. Any disagreement goes to Resolve.
From a real run
Measured
In version 2, all 15 of the verifier's independent test citizens agreed with the new rules.
6. Resolve
i
What happens
A coordinator rereads the disputed clause and decides: the encoder is wrong (send a precise fix), the verifier is wrong (accept with a reason), or the clause is genuinely ambiguous (ask a human).
Why it is needed
Some clauses can be read two ways. Guessing could stop people being paid.
What can go wrong
Recovery
A disagreement that survives a fix is escalated instead of retried. We added this after the version 1 traces showed one case going round three times.
From a real run
Measured
Whether the original order's "pay the difference" rule still applies after the amendment is now flagged as a question for a human.
7. Publish
i
What happens
Niyam commits the change (Entire links the coding agent's full session as a checkpoint), opens a pull request with quotes, verification, confidence and reasons, and merges on its own only when the trust policy allows.
Why it is needed
Every change is visible and reviewable, and its reasoning can be audited months later.
What can go wrong
Recovery
If GitHub is unreachable the job keeps its state and resumes later.
From a real run
Measured
The amendment went to human review, because one change ("Rs 1,500 or more" instead of "more than Rs 1,500") removes some people from the scheme.

Errors are JSON: {"error": {"code", "message", "docs_url"}}. Codes include invalid_key, rate_limited (with Retry-After), daily_limit, personal_data_rejected (a value looked like an Aadhaar or phone number), not_pdf, too_large.

Limits
No key: 30 requests per minute, 3 documents per day.
Free key: 120 requests per minute, 20 documents per day.

Privacy by design

The API never needs names, Aadhaar numbers or phone numbers, and rejects values that look like them. Eligibility requests are not stored, only counted.

Python: verify a webhook
Copy
import hashlib, hmac

def is_from_niyam(raw_body: bytes, signature_header: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret.encode(), raw_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature_header)

Happy path, real document

On the real amendment with a broken model output and an unusable text layer injected on purpose, Niyam repaired the output (recovery.json_repair), transcribed the PDF (recovery.ocr_fallback) and still scored 100% on outcomes, for $0.80. Verifier rejection, then a fix

Done
Version 1: the verifier disagreed on one case, the coordinator sent a fix, and the traces showed the same case looping. Version 2 adds the missing context and a loop guard. Full story in the build log.

Calibrated autonomy

Done
Acts alone only when a number or date changes and every check agrees. Never removes people from a scheme without a human. i On a labelled synthetic order that only adds people (age limit 60 to 62), 2 of 2 runs decided to act alone (dry run, never merged into the public rulebook). On the real amendment, which removes some people, every run asked a human.

A second real scheme, and a real order it may merge alone

Done
On an operator's request, Niyam onboarded Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Anudan Yojana from the real 56-page 2019 consolidated GR (PR #3, 49 tests). On top of it, the real 6 July 2023 order raising assistance to Rs 1,500 was judged safe to merge alone: only amounts rise, every independent check agrees, confidence 0.98, $0.20 in a dry run. Run live, the same order raised a question about widows with three or more children and went to a human instead (PR #4, since merged): 2 of 3 runs would have acted alone, and the third chose the safe path. Reviewing PR #3 also caught a real encoding mistake (a default that widened eligibility), fixed before merge.

A whole scheme from its founding order

Done
Starting from an empty rulebook with only the real 28 June 2024 Marathi GR, Niyam recognised a new scheme, extracted 19 rules, wrote the rulebook and tests, and passed 25 of 25 of our hand-written baseline test citizens, which it never saw. $0.81, 201 s. Checkpoint 01M4JFNT0M069MG48K0FT9V50P.

Planning	Each job runs a fixed plan of seven stages; the coordinator plans fixes when agents disagree.
Tool use	PDF reading and transcription, a citation checker, git worktrees, Claude Code, the rulebook test runner, simulation, GitHub.
State	Every state is saved before the next step. A failed run retried from its last good state (job_20261010_8b7a02ea).
Context	Triage reads 3 pages; the encoder sees only the checked change list; v2 added the missing benefit formula after the traces showed it was needed.
Execution	Watcher every 15 minutes; full runs of 1 to 3 minutes without a person.
Recovery	Transcription fallback for scans, schema repair, model fallback, encoder retries, budget stop, loop guard, resume.
Verification	A blind verifier on a different model writes its own test citizens; quotes are checked against the PDF; every change has boundary tests.

Pick any question from the list. Each answer takes about a minute to read. The glossary at the end explains every term.

What is Niyam, in one paragraph?
What is a welfare scheme?
What is a GR?
What does "rules as code" mean?
What is an AI agent, and how is it different from a chatbot?
What is a trace?
What is a checkpoint?
How does Niyam check its own work?
When does Niyam ask a human?
Why does this matter? Lessons from Robodebt and Samagra Vedika
Glossary
References
What is Niyam, in one paragraph?

Governments in India publish their welfare rules as orders, often PDF files in Marathi or Hindi. Apps, helplines and field workers then have to copy those rules by hand, and they often fall behind. Niyam is an AI helper that reads each new order, works out exactly what changed, updates one open set of rules with tests, and has a second AI check the work. A person approves anything risky. Anyone can then check their eligibility, and every answer shows the sentence of the government order it comes from.

What is a welfare scheme?
i

A government programme that gives people money, food, services or support if they meet certain conditions, such as age, income or where they live. Those conditions are called eligibility rules. For example, the Ladki Bahin scheme in Maharashtra pays eligible women Rs 1,500 a month.

What is a GR?
i

A Government Resolution is an official order from a state government department. GRs create schemes and change their rules: raising an age limit, changing an income ceiling, adding or removing a condition. Maharashtra publishes them as PDF files, mostly in Marathi, on its GR portal. Each has an 18-digit code, for example 202407031335114330.

What does "rules as code" mean?
i

Writing the rules of a scheme as a small computer program instead of only as text. The program applies the rules the same way every time, can be tested with example people, and can be read by anyone. Governments in France, New Zealand, Canada and elsewhere have explored this. Niyam stores rules as readable YAML files, in the format of OpenFisca, an open-source project, with a start date and a source for every value.

What is an AI agent, and how is it different from a chatbot?
i

A chatbot answers a question. An agent is given a goal and works towards it on its own: it plans steps, uses tools (reading files, running tests, opening change requests), looks at the results, and decides what to do next, including how to recover when something fails. Niyam's goal is: keep the rulebook in line with every new government order.

What is a trace?
i

A step-by-step recording of everything an agent did in one run: every AI model call, every tool, every retry, how long each took and what it cost. Niyam uses neatlogs for this. Traces are how we found and fixed a costly loop in version 1.

What is a checkpoint?
i

When code changes, the change itself is saved in git, but the reasoning behind it usually is not. Entire saves the AI agent's whole working session (what it was asked, what it read, what it tried) and links it to the code change. In Niyam, that means every rule has a record of why it says what it says.

How does Niyam check its own work?
i

A second agent, which never sees the code change, reads the government order and writes its own test people: "a 65-year-old woman with an income of Rs 2 lakh should be eligible". Those people are run through the new rules. If the two agents disagree, a coordinator rereads the clause and either fixes the rules or asks a human.

When does Niyam ask a human?
i

Whenever a clause is unclear, the two agents still disagree, confidence is below 0.90, or a change would remove people from a scheme. Only simple changes, such as a new amount or date with every check agreeing, are merged automatically. See the trust policy.

Why does this matter? Lessons from Robodebt and Samagra Vedika

In Australia, the Robodebt scheme used code that did not match the law and sent unlawful debt notices to hundreds of thousands of people; it led to a Royal Commission. In Telangana, the Samagra Vedika system cancelled more than 1.8 million food cards, and officials often deferred to the machine. In both cases, the people affected could not see why the system decided as it did. Niyam is built the other way round: every rule is open, sourced, tested and explained.

Glossary
Agent
Software that takes a goal, plans steps, uses tools and checks its own work.
API
A way for other software to ask Niyam questions over the internet.
API key
A secret code that identifies an app using the API.
Boundary case
A test exactly at a limit, such as age 65 when the limit is 65.
Checkpoint
The saved reasoning behind a code change (Entire).
Citation
The exact words, page and clause of a government order that a rule comes from.
Confidence
Niyam's score from 0 to 1 for how sure it is that a change is correct.
Eligibility
Whether a person meets the conditions of a scheme.
Encode
Turn a rule written in words into rule code.
Evaluation
A test of the whole agent on documents with known correct answers.
GR
Government Resolution: an official order from a state department.
MCP
Model Context Protocol: a standard way for AI assistants to use tools.
OCR or transcription
Turning a scanned page (an image) into text.
Parameter
A number or list in a rule that can change over time, such as the maximum age.
Pull request
A proposed change to code that can be reviewed before it is accepted.
Rulebook
The collection of all encoded rules, with tests and sources.
Trace
A step-by-step record of an agent run (neatlogs).
Triage
Quickly deciding whether a document matters.
Verifier
The independent agent that checks new rules against the law.
Webhook
A message Niyam can send to your system when a rule changes.
References

/trust/.text:
TRUST AND LIMITS

An agent you can trust to run without watching, and when it will not act alone
Wrongly removing someone from a welfare scheme causes real harm. Niyam is built to be fast for simple changes and careful for everything else.

About this page

EN
हिं
मरा

Niyam is a free tool that keeps the rules of government welfare schemes up to date, and shows the official source of every rule.

WHAT IS THIS PAGE?
When Niyam changes rules on its own, when it asks a person first, and what it never does.
WHO IS IT FOR?
Anyone deciding whether to trust Niyam's answers.
WHAT TO DO HERE
Read the three levels first. They explain exactly when a person must approve a change.

Want to know if you can get money from a scheme? Check your eligibility in 2 minutes

When Niyam acts alone
i

Every rule change is first written as a proposal. Applying it to the official rulebook is called merging i. Confidence i is Niyam's own score from 0 to 1 for how sure it is that the change matches the law.

Apply the change by itself

Only a number or a date changes, nobody loses eligibility, every quote is found in the order, every independent test agrees, and confidence is 0.90 or more.

Ask a person to review first

A condition is added, removed or reworded, a sentence could be read two ways, or confidence is from 0.70 up to (not including) 0.90.

Stop and ask a question

The two agents still disagree, confidence is below 0.70, or the run reaches its cost limit.

Hard rules on top: a change that removes people from a scheme always goes to a human. Uploaded documents run on a sandbox branch and are never merged.

What Niyam never does
Decide anyone's application. The government department decides.
Ask for or store names, Aadhaar numbers, phone numbers or addresses.
Get around a CAPTCHA i or a login on a government website.
Obey instructions hidden inside a document i. The coding agent only ever sees a checked list of changes, never the raw document. We tested this with a hidden instruction to raise the income limit: Niyam ignored it and changed nothing.
Edit or delete history. Old values stay, so the rules on any past date can be checked.
Your data
The eligibility checker on this site runs in your browser. Nothing is sent.
The API rejects values that look like ID or phone numbers, and stores only request counts.
Uploaded documents are processed on a test copy i and should not contain personal information.
API keys are stored only in a scrambled form (a hash) that cannot be turned back into the key.
No cookies, no tracking.

Found a wrong rule?

Every rule shows its source, so you can check it against the law yourself. To report a mistake, fill in this short form on GitHub (a free GitHub account is needed): write the scheme, the rule, and what the government order says.

Disclaimer

Niyam is an independent project built at neatHack 2026. It is not an official government service. Information only; the government department makes the final decision.
